identity.mechanic: Vigil N: effect. The unit keeps a count that starts at N. Start of Turn: it counts down by 1. When it reaches 0, the Vigil **ends**: the effect happens and the count goes back to N. A Vigil counts only while its unit is on your board. All Vigils count down together; the ones that end resolve in reading order. A Vigil ends at most once a turn: after it ends, it doesn't count down again until next turn. A unit holds at most one Vigil.

keywords.name: Deep Vigil N
keywords.text: A Vigil that also counts down by 1 each time another of your Vigils ends (but not when another Deep Vigil ends).

keywords.name: Dripstone
keywords.text: How many of your Vigils have ended this game. It never goes down. When a Vigil ends, Dripstone rises first, then the effect happens. A repeated effect (Brother Netopir) is not an ending: it adds no Dripstone and ticks no Deep Vigil.

identity.plays: The olms are pale, slow and weak for a long time. Each of them sits on a countdown and does one thing when it finishes. Every finish lays down a little Dripstone, and the tribe's payoffs grow with that stone: Olmlings that grow a little more with each Vigil, a "Baby Dragon" whose bite is the rumour's age, an Eldest whose rare answer lifts the whole board. The puzzle is clock work: short Vigils pay often and feed the stone and the Deep Vigils; tools that ring, knock or flood make clocks finish early; bats repeat whatever was said last; and a lamplighter hangs Vigils on units of other tribes, which can't see that they're being enlisted. Against all that, a robber-knight pays you to keep quiet, and an old sitter makes every Vigil longer and louder, so a board can be built to speak often or to speak rarely and hugely.

units.golden: Vigil 3: permanently gain +2/+2 for each Dripstone.

units.name: Kurent Bell-Runner
units.text: When played: your Vigils count down by 1.
units.golden: When played: your Vigils count down by 2.

units.name: Courier Bat

units.name: Lamplighter Hrošč

units.name: Guild Knocker

units.golden: Vigil 2: your other Vigils count down by 2.

units.name: Comes-and-Goes Olm
units.text: Vigil 2: your units permanently gain +2 Health if your lake is in, or +2 Attack if it is out. Then your lake turns. (You have one lake, shared by all these Vigils and shown on your board. It starts in.)
units.golden: Vigil 2: your units permanently gain +4 Health if your lake is in, or +4 Attack if it is out. Then your lake turns. (You have one lake, shared by all these Vigils and shown on your board. It starts in.)

units.name: "Baby Dragon"
units.text: Start of Combat: gain +1 Attack for each Dripstone.

units.name: Pilgrim of the Still Pool
units.text: After one of your Vigils ends, give that unit +3/+3 permanently.

units.name: Scribe of the Echo Nave
units.text: When played: give a unit without a Vigil a copy of another unit's Vigil (not a Deep Vigil), with a full count.

units.name: Brother Netopir
units.text: End of Turn, after your Vigils count down: repeat the effect of the last unit whose Vigil ended this turn.
units.golden: End of Turn, after your Vigils count down: repeat the effect of the last unit whose Vigil ended this turn, twice.

units.name: The Robber-Knight
units.text: Swoop. End of Turn, after your other effects: if none of your Vigils ended this turn, gain 3 gold.

units.name: Parkelj the Dark

units.golden: Your Vigils also count down by 2 at End of Turn, before your other End of Turn effects.

units.name: The Seven-Year Sitter
units.text: Your other units' Vigils are 1 longer, and the stats and gold their Vigil effects give are doubled. (Count-downs, cards gotten and "for every N" don't change.)
units.golden: Your other units' Vigils are 2 longer, and the stats and gold their Vigil effects give are tripled. (Count-downs, cards gotten and "for every N" don't change.)

units.name: Flood-Mark Reader

units.name: The Eldest

units.name: Mother Ribica

builds.name: The long count (Dripstone)
builds.text: Lots of short Vigils: Old Polh, Hrošč's lamps, Guild Knockers, Scribe copies of Vigil 2 effects, with Parkelj doubling the rate. The stone climbs by 3–6 a turn, and you cash it in with Olmlings, "Baby Dragon", the Flood-Mark Reader, the Eldest and the Dragon Under the Earth. Spike's line: steady, readable growth.

builds.name: The clutch (goldens)
builds.text: Mother Ribica's Deep Vigil 12 never finishes on its own. Feed it endings: two Knockers ending each other (each Vigil ends once a turn), Spring-Spilled Olms, lamps on everything. Every clutch gives a golden copy of your best unit, and playing a golden Discovers from the tier above. The Spring-Spilled Olm makes Olmling triples on the side. Johnny's line: the high roll is a golden Brother Netopir, or Netopir repeating Ribica when hers is the last Vigil to end.

builds.name: The quiet house (pulse)
builds.text: The Robber-Knight pays 3 gold for a silent turn, and the Seven-Year Sitter makes Vigils longer and twice as loud. Set all your Vigils to the same length so they end on the same turn: one loud turn, then quiet paid turns. Netopir repeats the loud turn's best effect (for example a doubled Comes-and-Goes Olm). Parkelj and Kurents break the rhythm, so this build leaves them out or times them on purpose.

builds.name: Lamps for strangers (cross-tribe)
builds.text:
Hrošč and the Scribe hang Vigils on another tribe's carry or on neutral units. The Comes-and-Goes Olm and the Eldest buff every unit, not just olms, so the olm core can sit behind someone else's main plan.
- *Oozes:* eat the Dragon Under the Earth for its stone-swollen stats, or Belly a big Olmling to keep it safe (its Vigil pauses).
- *Hedgerow:* a lamp on your rightmost unit stacks with Pass. The Courier Bat's "next to" growth pays for a dense touching run.
- *Bog folk:* the lake's Health turns a Mire unit into a wall. The Pilgrim makes a lamp-lit Mire unit grow with each ending.
- *Fairies:* the Dragon counts as a Fairy for Ring cards. Old Polh's gold pays for aimed spells on Shy units. (The Dragon is a Fairy, but it isn't Shy.)
- *Birds:* the Dragon counts as a Bird and so can Fly South. Its stats are real and permanent, so it comes home doubled. Vigils on a Bird pause while it is away.
- *Hunters:* the Robber-Knight's Swoop plus Quarry splits their targets. The lake's Attack turns go to Pack units.

risks: **Slow start.** Before turn 4 only the Kurent and the 2/2 Olmling are real bodies. If early losses cost too much Health, give the Kurent +1 Health.

**Counter load.** Up to seven countdowns, a Dripstone total and the lake all at once. The screen has to show each count and the next ending clearly (Mother Ribica's count large), mark the unit Netopir will repeat, and show the lake on the board, or the tribe becomes bookkeeping.

**Chain resolution.** Knockers, Parkelj and Deep Vigils can set off cascades. Each Vigil ends at most once a turn, so every cascade stops. At End of Turn, count-downs (Parkelj) resolve first, then Netopir's repeat, then the Robber-Knight's check. The order inside a cascade still needs an animation players can read.

**Netopir on capstones.** Repeating Ribica gives two goldens a turn at most, and repeating the Eldest doubles a +10/+10 board buff. It is a deliberate high roll, but if it decides lobbies, exclude Deep Vigil effects from repeats.
**The Dragon counts as every tribe.** Every other tribe's text needs a check against it: Fly South, Shy, Ring and Eat edge cases. It may be the most rules-heavy line in the game.

**Lamps leak power.** Lamps on neutral and other-tribe units may make the Olm Sleepers' best units splash too well into other builds. Watch whether Hrošč and the Scribe get picked up by other tribes' players.
**The Sitter's doubling** covers only stats and gold. Check that a golden Olmling under the Sitter, repeated by Netopir, doesn't run away by round 12.
**Dripstone never falls.** Late-game Olmlings grow quadratically. That is the fantasy, but check round 12+ board totals against other tribes.

tier_check.note: The Olmling seed gives about 0.8 body a turn at Dripstone 5, twice the guide's 0.4 by mid-game and more later. This is on purpose: it's weak early and is the tribe's "then devastating" card. The Kurent is a 5-stat tempo body with a small tick.
Polh averages 1 gold a turn, plus Dripstone. The Courier Bat gives 2–4 stats a turn. Hrošč's lamp gives 2 a turn, plus a Dripstone source anywhere. All sit inside 0.3–1 body.

The Comes-and-Goes Olm gives about 6 a turn (0.85 body). "Baby Dragon" gets +8 Attack in a fight at Dripstone 8 (1.1 body). The Knocker and Spring-Spilled Olm are enablers, priced in endings and in Olmlings for triples.

The Pilgrim gives 12–18 a turn (1.4–2 bodies), at the generous end. Netopir is the first multiplier. The Robber-Knight averages about 1.5 gold a turn, in a build that gives up Dripstone to get it. The Scribe doubles a Vigil once.

Parkelj roughly doubles the ending rate, a multiplier in place of a flat amount. The Reader gives about 50 in a fight at Dripstone 15 (4 bodies). The Sitter is the direction card, a trade more than a gain.

The Eldest gives about 60 a turn, rising to about 120 with Parkelj (4–8 bodies, under the "top ~10"). Ribica's golden every 2–3 turns is the capstone high roll. The Dragon gives about 70 once at Dripstone 18 (5 bodies), on a deliberately small 10-stat body, plus about 12 a turn.

rationale: The Eldest "last spoke before anyone's grandmother hatched": the tribe speaks rarely, so its basic unit of play is a countdown that pays out (Vigil).
Dripstone "grows more slowly than an olm ages": a total of endings that never falls. It gives patience a number that payoffs can read.
Mother Ribica's once-a-dozen-years clutch was too slow on its own, so Deep Vigil counts down on other endings. That made the core puzzle: short clocks feed long ones.
The Kurent's cowbells wake sleepers: a cheap count-down tool, and the T1 tempo body the slow tribe needs.
Brother Netopir, "loyal to whoever asked last": he repeats the last effect, which turns the order of endings into a puzzle.
Hrošč's lamps "nobody in the order can see": they go only on units without a Vigil. That makes the lamplighter the cross-tribe enabler, and Parkelj, the olm who can see, can take one.
The Robber-Knight pays the order to keep quiet: gold for silent turns, a rival plan to piling up Dripstone.
The olm that "stayed in the same spot for seven years": the Seven-Year Sitter makes Vigils longer and louder, a choice of direction rather than raw power.
"They never correct anyone about the dragon thing": "Baby Dragon" bites by the age of the rumour, and the Dragon Under the Earth counts as every tribe.
The Comes-and-Goes Lake: a buff that alternates between Health and Attack, which gives players a timing choice.
Repeats and Deep-from-Deep endings don't count, which keeps every cascade finite.
Kept the default tier shape, because the guide's roles mapped cleanly onto the figures from the seed.

changes.what: Vigil keyword: a Vigil ends at most once a turn, then stops counting until next turn.
changes.why: Knocker Vigils could end each other forever, giving endless Ribica goldens; now every cascade stops.
The tribe had almost no early body; one more Attack helps the first fights without changing its growth.

changes.what: One lake per player, shared by every Comes-and-Goes Vigil and shown on the board.
changes.why: It didn't say whose lake it was; a shared lake makes two copies a timing puzzle.

changes.what: Repeats the effect of the last unit whose Vigil ended, after count-downs resolve.
changes.why: "Last effect" was hard to track in a cascade and could miss Parkelj's End of Turn endings.

changes.what: Its End of Turn count-down now resolves before other End of Turn effects.
changes.why: So Netopir and the Robber-Knight see the endings it causes; the order was unwritten.

changes.what: Says exactly what doubles: stats and gold given. Count-downs, cards gotten and "for every N" don't.
changes.why: "Numbers doubled" couldn't be read on the Eldest, Ribica or the Knocker.
